title: Chocolate-Dipped Shortbread
changes_from_base: No sugar sprinkle; the cooled fingers are half-dipped in dark chocolate (melted, then seeded with chopped chocolate).
summary: Follows the classic butter shortbread method, skipping the sugar sprinkle so the cooled fingers can be half-dipped in melted dark chocolate instead.
equipment: 20 cm square metal baking tin (not glass), lined with a baking-paper sling
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) for at least 20 minutes before baking, ideally during the dough's chilling time.

steps.title: Cream butter and sugar
steps.text: Beat the cool-soft butter with the sugar and salt for 2-3 minutes until pale and creamy, but not fluffy or white. Overbeating whips in too much air and softens the characteristic short, dense crumb.

steps.title: Add flour and cornflour
steps.text: Sift in the flour and cornflour and mix on low speed or with a spatula only until the dough clumps together. With no egg or leavening in the mix, handling it as little as possible keeps it short rather than tough.

steps.title: Press into the tin
steps.text: Press the dough evenly into the lined 20cm metal tin and smooth flat, then prick all over with a fork so steam can escape evenly as it bakes.

steps.title: Chill the dough
steps.text: Chill for 30 minutes until firm, so it holds its shape and bakes evenly.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake for 35-40 minutes, until pale to just golden all over and a touch deeper at the edges, but never properly brown. Long, gentle heat dries and crisps the biscuit without the colour running away.

steps.title: Cut while warm
steps.text: Cool for 5-10 minutes, then cut into 16 fingers while still warm in the tin — cold shortbread cracks under the knife rather than slicing cleanly. Skip the sugar sprinkle this time, since the chocolate coating finishes it.

steps.title: Cool fully
steps.text: Leave to cool completely in the tin before lifting the fingers out.

steps.title: Melt and seed the chocolate
steps.text: Once the fingers are completely cold, melt 100g of the chocolate gently in a bowl over barely simmering water, without the bowl touching the water. Take it off the heat and stir in the remaining 50g chopped chocolate until smooth and slightly cooled — this seeding helps it set glossy with a clean snap.

steps.title: Dip and set
steps.text: Dip one end of each finger into the melted chocolate, let the excess drip off, and set on baking paper. Leave to set for 1 hour at a cool room temperature, or 15 minutes in the fridge, until the chocolate is firm.

tips: Seed the melted chocolate with the reserved chopped chocolate rather than using it straight from melting — it sets glossy and snaps cleanly instead of staying soft and dull.
Make sure the shortbread is completely cold before dipping, or the chocolate will melt back off instead of setting onto the surface.
Stop creaming once the butter and sugar look pale and creamy, not fluffy white, to keep that classic dense, short crumb.
Let the dipped fingers set undisturbed on baking paper — moving them too soon smears the chocolate before it firms up.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep in an airtight tin at room temperature for 3-4 days. It freezes well for up to 2 months; thaw at room temperature before serving.
